The short version

Umi has a strong POS core inside a thin ecosystem

The five competitors sell the same shape: one connected data graph (item, category, order, customer) that feeds a register, a kitchen display, online ordering, loyalty, and reporting, plus first-party payments and hardware. Category is the shared key for kitchen routing and reports. Payments and lending are the money engine. Toast now adds an agentic AI layer (Toast IQ) across the whole stack.

Umi's transaction core is real and certified for pilot: sale, catalog, checkout, cash, and refunds/voids all passed gated validation. The dashboard is backed by real endpoints, not mock data. The known cash-shift and refund RLS bugs are fixed in code.

Where Umi is short of an "ecosystem":

  • No real payment gateway — tenders are manual/attested only.
  • No online/web ordering channel (only POS + WhatsApp write orders).
  • No POS-sales analytics rollup — owner "revenue" is a loyalty top-up proxy.
  • The real KDS is still the legacy SwiftUI app; the Flutter KDS is a read-only preview.
  • Loyalty backend exists, but has no tiers, reward catalog, or enable switch.

Umi's real edge to defend: native-first, hardware-backed device identity and offline. Every competitor is cloud-dependent. Square times out card mode in one hour; Toast needs a Local Hub; Lightspeed and Odoo are register-centric offline. Umi has an encrypted offline journal with idempotent replay and device proof-of-possession. Add a Spanish-first, WhatsApp-native, LatAm posture, and PoloTab is the only direct comparable — and PoloTab has no loyalty, no gift cards, and no self-order kiosk.

The five ecosystems

How each competitor packages the whole system

Each teardown lists the positioning, the packaging model, the strongest capabilities, and the seam that Umi can attack. Dots rate breadth: ● strong, ● partial, ● thin or none. Screenshots are the live pages captured on 2026-09-06.

Lightspeed K-Series · iPad

A modular cloud platform. A thin, low-priced core POS, plus revenue from attach modules and tier upgrades. Everything routes through a cloud Back Office; the iPad POS must "reload" to pull config.

POS & tables KDS 2.0 Order Anywhere Loyalty (native) Payments Inventory/recipes Benchmarks API (Premium)
  • KDS 2.0 is mature: color status flow, per-station routing by item/group/category, wait-time SLA pulses, a POS↔KDS status mirror that pushes "Ready" back to online-ordering partners.
  • Delivery is a real differentiator: own-fleet self-delivery plus Uber Direct white-label at 0% commission, positioned against marketplaces.
  • Inventory add-on has ingredient recipes, production batches, purchase orders, and par levels. Advanced Insights benchmarks a venue against anonymized peers.
  • Pricing stacks: $69 Starter → $189 Essential → $399 Premium, plus KDS $30/screen, Order Anywhere, Inventory, Reservations layered on top. Processing rates are never published.
Seam for Umi Payments + hardware lock-in with hidden rates; everything-is-an-add-on TCO; Apple/iPad-only stack; native loyalty is card-batch only and real loyalty is outsourced to Marsello.

Toast Vertical restaurant OS

Proprietary hardware + POS + processing + a full SaaS suite (kitchen, ordering, marketing, payroll, inventory, capital), all on one back office ("Toast Web"). Monetized on processing spread, add-ons, hardware, and lending.

POS & coursing KDS (enterprise) Online order & pay Loyalty/Marketing Payments Hardware+network xtraCHEF inventory Public API + AI
  • KDS is the bar to clear: assembly lines (item traverses ordered stations), load balancing across duplicate screens, partial fulfillment, food-runner mode, on-screen recipes, All-Day view.
  • Offline is the reference design: per-device detection, a Local Hub that relays orders across the LAN with no internet, card payments via background auth on reconnect.
  • Toast IQ (AI) answers business questions and takes permission-scoped actions — edits menus, prep stations, campaigns, schedules. This is the newest strategic threat.
  • Platform: documented REST API across 18+ domains, outbound loyalty/gift APIs, webhooks, an 8-stage partner certification, and a public marketplace.
Seam for Umi Marketing/CRM depth is soft (no DKIM, no reward stacking); scheduling is weakly tied to payroll; cost is pushed onto processing rates; kiosk lacks upsell.

Square Connected cloud graph

One cloud graph across POS, online, kiosk, KDS, and delivery, with Category as the routing + reporting key. Since Oct 2025, three plans (Free / Plus $49 / Premium $149 per location), but KDS and Kiosk are per-device add-ons on top.

Restaurants POS KDS (Android) Online + QR Loyalty+Marketing Payments+Afterpay Hardware+Kiosk Inventory (partner) Open API
  • Menu ingestion by photo/PDF upload, AI starter generation, or import from Toast/DoorDash. Conversational modifiers and nested sets cut kitchen errors.
  • Loyalty ↔ Marketing ↔ CRM is one native loop on a free Customer Directory, with new VIP tiers and automations (welcome, birthday, win-back).
  • Genuinely open platform: 20+ APIs, 100+ endpoints, SDKs, webhooks, and an app marketplace (DoorDash, Uber Eats, MarketMan, Mailchimp).
  • Weak spot: offline is cloud-dependent — card window one hour, must reconnect within 24 hours, seller carries all risk, no live menu/inventory/KDS sync.
Seam for Umi Time-boxed cloud offline; per-location + per-device pricing that compounds; coursing/seat tracking gated to Premium; no native recipe inventory (MarketMan +$99); iPad POS but Android-only KDS.

Odoo All-in-one ERP

An open-source ERP of ~50 apps sharing one database. POS is one module that inherits products, customers, stock, accounting, loyalty, and eCommerce from the rest. Priced per user for all apps, not per terminal.

POS + restaurant Preparation Display eCommerce + kiosk Loyalty (unified) Payments (partners) IoT hardware Full WMS API + Studio
  • Breadth is the edge: one DB unifies POS, online store, loyalty, inventory, HR, and native double-entry accounting. Session close posts journal entries automatically.
  • Cross-channel loyalty and promotions (cards, coupons, gift cards, eWallet, pricelists) are shared by Sales, eCommerce, and POS.
  • Studio is no-code customization with automation rules and Python server actions. External API by XML-RPC/JSON-RPC + webhooks.
  • Weakness: hospitality depth and polish are generic; the prep display is browser-only; hardware is generic via an IoT box; delivery is a third-party connector.
Seam for Umi Generic table/KDS UX; no hardware-attested device identity; key features are Enterprise-gated; running an ERP has real operational overhead and upgrade friction.

PoloTab Mexico · direct comparable

A Mexico-only POS + restaurant platform for cafés and restaurants, sold as bundled proprietary hardware + software. Claims 900+ venues, 22.8M orders/yr, 100% offline. Wedge: human 24/7 Spanish support "in an age full of bots." This is Umi's design north-star.

Fast POS + modifiers KDS time-ramp Delivery aggregation Loyalty / gift PoloPay Own hardware Inventory + costing Report "Playground"
  • Design language (the north-star): near-black operational apps with a single vivid blue (~#0066FF); three-pane POS with a colored-bar category rail; bottom tabs Comanda / Mesas / Ventas / Ajustes; inline modifier picker with required/max + upcharge.
  • KDS ticket header ramps by elapsed time (gray→yellow→orange→red); size modifier in blue; near-zero chrome. Customer display is personalized ("¡Hola, Marco!"); the tender screen floods full blue.
  • Native delivery aggregation of Uber Eats, Rappi, DiDi Food into one screen; menu/price/photo sync back in seconds. Deep inventory with recipes, costing, waste, and 2-click inter-branch transfers.
  • Back office is a light SaaS dashboard: a custom report builder ("Playground"), saved reports, PoP/YoY, profit/COGS, and a Trazabilidad audit log.
Seam for Umi No loyalty, no gift cards, no promotions engine, no own-brand web storefront, and no self-order kiosk. Mexico-only. Umi can match the aesthetic and beat it on loyalty + WhatsApp identity + stored value.

Roadmap says "complete" — code says "certified pilot, thin ecosystem"

Umi's own roadmap marks Gates 2A–12 complete (POS, cash, refunds, inventory, loyalty, KDS, dashboard), with Gate 13 (real hardware + providers) deferred. That grade is fair for the pilot transaction system. It does not mean the ecosystem breadth that Toast/Square/Lightspeed sell is present.

Code hygiene is high

The audit found no NotImplemented and no "not implemented" throws in production code, and one environmental skipped test. Incompleteness is missing features and unset config, not half-written code. That is a healthy base to build the ecosystem on.

What is needed yet

Prioritized build backlog

Ordered by how much each item blocks a real, sellable ecosystem. Each item states the work, the reason, and where it lands in the code.

P0 Blocks a real ecosystem

Integrated payment gateway

Add real card auth / capture / settlement, surcharge, and payment-level refund. Today tenders are cash and manual_terminal, with status hardcoded to captured.

Why: every competitor monetizes on processing. Without it, Umi cannot take a card or earn the spread. Where: pos-checkout.repository.ts, 32_pos_checkout.sql, contract tenders.

Real KDS station: device role + Flutter board

Add a device-role attribute, an unattended KDS station session, multi-column board with per-item state and timers, ticket commands, and an event stream that replaces the poll. Then retire the SwiftUI umi-kds at parity.

Why: KDS is table-stakes and Toast/Lightspeed set a high bar. Umi's board is a 5% preview. Where: kitchen_board_surface.dart, credential_vault.dart, umi_contract.dart.

Sales analytics rollup

Build a POS-sales read model: net sales, product mix, category, daypart, employee, and per-café + chain rollups with PoP/YoY.

Why: owner "revenue" is a loyalty top-up proxy; PoloTab's "Playground" and Square/Toast reports are a core owner value. Where: new API read model + dashboard overview.jsx.

P1 Closes the biggest competitive gaps

Online + QR ordering channel

Add a web order writer and a QR order-and-pay flow that lands orders in the POS and KDS like in-house orders. The order seam already reserves the enum.

Why: a commission-free branded channel is the standard anti-marketplace wedge. Where: shared/orders/order-writer.ts.

Loyalty tiers, reward catalog, and enable switch

Add membership tiers, a points-reward catalog CRUD, an owner enablement surface, and birthday + points-expiry crons. The ledger already exists.

Why: loyalty is on but off by flag; tiers and rewards are what drive repeat visits. This also beats PoloTab, which has no loyalty. Where: merchant.loyalty_*, dashboard loyalty hub.

Offline auto-replay + real connectivity source

Add an OS-level connectivity source and automatic journal replay on reconnect, decoupled from the catalog screen.

Why: offline is Umi's headline edge; it must drain without operator action to beat Square's time-boxed model. Where: platform_adapters.dart.

POS/KDS realtime + Redis adapter

Move POS and KDS from polling to Socket.IO event streams and add a Redis adapter for multi-replica scale-out.

Why: polling caps kitchen responsiveness and blocks horizontal scale. Where: realtime gateway, realtime-channels.ts.

Persist order type; delivery aggregation

Save the order-type pill to the sale, then add delivery aggregation (Uber Eats / Rappi / DiDi) into POS + KDS, as PoloTab does for the LatAm market.

Why: order type drives routing, tax, and reports; delivery aggregation is expected in Mexico. Where: catalog_surface.dart, orders module.

P2 Depth, polish, and platform

Marketing (email / SMS / WhatsApp campaigns)

Add campaigns and automated segments on top of the customer model, using WhatsApp identity as the channel edge no competitor has.

Why: Square and Toast bundle marketing; Umi's WhatsApp spine is a stronger, cheaper channel. Where: customers + automations worker.

Merge-candidate detector; update the stale skill doc

Add automatic duplicate-customer detection (the count is hardcoded to 0) and fix the customer-identity-resolution skill, which still describes the retired platform.contacts schema.

Why: clean identity is the base for loyalty and marketing. Where: identity.resolver.ts, skill doc.

Customer-display app mode + kitchen tickets

Promote the customer display from a simulator peripheral to a real device mode, and confirm whether kitchen-ticket printing is needed alongside the KDS.

Why: PoloTab's personalized customer display is a visible differentiator. Where: POS device modes, printer adapters.

Self-order kiosk; hardware attestation; wallet secrets; dashboard tail

Add a kiosk mode, real hardware attestation, wallet secret provisioning, and finish the dashboard redesign tail (retire the operations.jsx bridge, deepen the Overview cockpit, add screen-level tests, add an automations surface).

Why: these harden the platform and close small, visible gaps. Where: POS, devices, umi-dashboard.

Positioning

Where Umi should plant its flag

1. Own reliability

Native-first, hardware-backed, offline-complete. Make "it keeps selling with no internet, with no operator action" the promise. This is the one axis where Square is weak, Toast needs extra hardware, and Odoo/Lightspeed are register-only.

2. Own the LatAm café

Spanish-first, WhatsApp-native, transparent pricing. PoloTab proves the market and the aesthetic, but has no loyalty, gift, or storefront. Umi can match the design and beat the value.

3. Turn identity into loyalty

Umi already resolves customers by phone and WhatsApp. Ship tiers, rewards, and campaigns on that spine. No competitor has WhatsApp as a first-class identity + marketing channel.

4. Close the money loop

A real payment gateway plus a sales-analytics rollup turns the certified transaction core into a business the owner can run and Umi can monetize. These two unlock the rest.

Method, sources, and caveats

Competitor content was scraped from official help centers and product pages with WebFetch (page-to-markdown) and full-page Playwright screenshots on 2026-09-06. Toast's pos.toasttab.com returned HTTP 403 and was recovered via support/doc.toasttab.com and search. PoloTab's developer/API and G2 pages were JS-gated or bot-blocked; those cells are graded conservatively and third-party facts are labeled in the notes. The Umi audit used the CodeGraph index (1,140 files / 21,993 nodes), file reads, and SQL over the build-v3 schema. Raw per-competitor notes and per-domain audit notes are saved next to this report under sources/; screenshots are under assets/.
